gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the BLUETTI Elite 30 V2's '4.5 W standby' is the idle draw with only the AC output on, or that it doubles to 9 W when the DC outputs are also on. The 12 V tip (DC for the router, AC for the modem) therefore makes this unit's overhead worse: for a 20 W router and modem, estimated runtime falls from about 11.8 h to about 9.9 h.
standout_why: I compared homepowerfacts.com (cited), outagemath.com (cited), backupcalc.com (cited) and runtimewise.com (rank 5). Homepowerfacts gives idle draw only for 1 kWh-plus units and none for anything under 300 Wh. Outagemath says makers don't publish idle draw. Backupcalc says idle is 'often 10–30 W' and says to use 12 V DC to avoid it. Runtimewise covers no idle draw or switchover at all. None of the four gives a switchover time for any model. None says that turning on DC as well as AC adds overhead on some units. All four use a flat 85% efficiency factor.
decides: It keeps the Elite 30 V2 as the pick: it has the only small-unit idle figure split by output, and its ≤10 ms UPS claim is unambiguous. The EcoFlow RIVER 3's own figures conflict (StorageReview's spec table says <20 ms, its text says 10 ms), and Jackery's 240 v2 is 20 ms. It also changes the advice for the Elite 30 V2: put the router and modem on the same output type, so only one bank is on. Splitting them between AC and DC turns on both banks and costs about 2 hours at 20 W. One caveat: if ECO mode is on, it may cut AC at low load. I couldn't confirm that from the manual.

findings.label: No-load draw, AC output only
findings.source_title: Power Station vs UPS for a Homelab: Switchover Time and NUT Support (ComputingForGeeks, Valentine Cheronoh, updated 2026-10-19)
findings.note: ComputingForGeeks reports that BLUETTI lists 4.5 W with only AC on. This matches the 'only 4.5W standby' line on BLUETTI's US store page, but that page doesn't say which outputs it covers.

findings.label: No-load draw, AC and DC outputs both on
findings.source_title: Power Station vs UPS for a Homelab: Switchover Time and NUT Support (ComputingForGeeks, Valentine Cheronoh, updated 2026-10-19)
findings.note: ComputingForGeeks attributes the figure to BLUETTI. Estimated runtime = 288 Wh ÷ (load + idle draw). 20 W all on AC: 288 ÷ 24.5 = 11.8 h. 20 W split between AC and DC: 288 ÷ 29 = 9.9 h. Both figures leave out conversion losses that rise with load, so treat them as upper bounds.
